newsitem.title: USA: Newmont Mining boosts offer for Santa Fe.
newsitem.headline: Newmont Mining boosts offer for Santa Fe.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp said Tuesday it had raised its bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp to $16.50 per share, or about $2.2 billion based on Monday's closing stock prices.
The announcement confirmed news first learned by Reuters through a market source.
Newmont said it was offering 0.40 share of its stock for each Santa Fe share. Originally, on December 5, it offered 0.33 Newmont share for each Santa Fe share.
Newmont said its new offer was 12.8 percent above Homestake Mining Co's offer of 1.115 Homestake shares for each Santa Fe share.
On December 9 Santa Fe agreed to be acquired by Homestake. Based on market prices at that time, Homestake's offer valued Santa Fe at $17.42 per share, or $2.3 billion.

However, since then, Santa Fe shares have fallen about 13 percent, Homestake shares have fallen about nine percent, and Newmont shares have fallen about 12 percent -- all amid a decline in the price of gold of 2.4 percent, or $8.80 an ounce.
On Monday, Santa Fe closed at 14-1/4, Homestake closed at 13-1/8, and Newmont closed at 41-1/2.
In their December 9 pact, Santa Fe and Homestake agreed to a $65 million break-up fee to be paid if either party backed out of the deal.
Newmont, in announcing its increased offer, said its board had urged Santa Fe to terminate the deal with Homestake.

A Newmont-Santa Fe company would have more than $50 million a year in operating cost synergies, before a one-time transaction cost, Newmont said. The combined company would also have 50 million ounces in proven gold reserves, it said.
The acquisition would be accretive to Newmont's earnings in the first year after the close of the deal, Newmont added.

Newmont also said the acquisition would be accretive in terms of gold reserves immediately, and would be accretive in terms of production and cash flow per share in the second year following the close.

In a registration statement filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Newmont said it intended to commence an exchange offer for Santa Fe's approximately 133 million outstanding common shares on a fully diluted basis.
The offer will begin when the registration statement is declared effective by the SEC, it said.
It said its board had requested that Santa Fe enter into negotiations with Newmont.
Newmont said it is filing preliminary proxy materials with the SEC today to be used in connection with solicitation of Santa Fe shareholders against the merger with Homestake.
